Recent reports that Beyonce and Jay-Z were set to purchase the rights to the controversial Confederate flag have been dismissed.
Earlier this week, numerous news sources claimed that the couple were willing to pay $280 million (£180 million) to block the emblem’s future use.
The flag was used by the Confederate States of America during the US Civil War and has long been seen as a patriotic sign for the south of the country.
It has also been accused of bearing racist connotations due to the Confederate States’ history of slavery.
Website NewsWatch33 were the first to report that Jay Z and Beyoncé were considering the acquisition.

The source cited the couple’s supposed lawyer Ralph Hammerstein as saying: “If my clients are successful, purchasing the rights would mean anyone who wants to produce merchandise using the Confederate flag would have to get permission from Mr and Mrs Carter”.
However, Gawker have now reported that Hammerstein does not actually exist and that the story was fictional.
During his ‘Yeezus’ tour in 2013, Kanye West attempted to subvert the Confederate symbol, using it on a series of t-shirts and other merchandise.
West’s reappropriation of the Confederate flag was criticised by fellow rapper Q-Tip.
In defence of his merchandise and use of the image, Kanye spoke to radio station 97.1 AMP explaining he was trying to reclaim the symbol.
